clue.text: Taking turns to change a race

parts.note: to change something is to alter it
a race of people is a nation

explanation.surface: Someone rotates the job of changing a whole people.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing things one after another in sequence is the noun sense of a back-and-forth swap.

clue.text: Contract to build a flyover

parts.note: a flyover is a bridge carrying one road over another

explanation.surface: A construction firm signs a contract to build a road flyover.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Contract' reads as a noun for a building job, but it is the verb meaning shorten.
explanation.definitionFit: To shorten a text is to cut it down, a synonym of contract as a verb.

clue.text: Food for a tot's mashed up

indicators.note: mashed up suggests the letters of the words a tot's are crushed into a new order

explanation.surface: Something to eat for a toddler, all mashed up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mashed up' rearranges ATOTS, the letters of 'a tot's' (the apostrophe ignored).
explanation.definitionFit: Browned bread slices are a common item to eat.

clue.text: Urge to cut riverside growth-it must be controlled

indicators.note: to cut into a word means to be inserted in it, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: reeds are plants that grow along riverbanks
to urge someone is to press them

explanation.surface: A warning that the plants by the river need keeping in check.
explanation.walkthrough: 'it must be' is a link to the definition; 'riverside growth' is the reed plant of riverbanks.
explanation.definitionFit: Held back or kept in check is a synonym of restrained, i.e. controlled.

clue.text: The first man in had a marvellous innings

indicators.note: in tells us the letters sit inside the words had a marvellous, spanning them

explanation.surface: An opening batsman scored a superb innings in a cricket match.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' points into 'hAD A Marvellous'; the cricket 'innings' is surface dressing.
explanation.definitionFit: In Genesis the earliest human created was the biblical figure in Eden.

clue.text: Popular drink to give some get-up-and-go

parts.note: something popular is said to be in
a spirit is a strong alcoholic drink

explanation.surface: A fashionable tipple is said to perk people up.
explanation.definitionFit: To fill with courage or energy is to enliven someone, giving them vigour.

clue.text: Thing that appears quite different after sunset

indicators.note: appears quite different says the letters of thing are shown in another order

explanation.surface: Something that looks unlike itself once the sun has gone down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'appears quite different' rearranges the letters of 'Thing'.
explanation.definitionFit: The dark hours following dusk are the period of darkness, the time of day after sunset.

clue.text: Italian ninnies accepting refusal

indicators.note: accepting means one word takes in the other, holding it inside

parts.note: a goose is a silly person, so ninnies are geese
no is a refusal

explanation.surface: Some foolish Italians take a rejection on board.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ninnies' reads as describing the Italians, but supplies the wordplay; a goose is a fool.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone or something from Genoa, a port city of northern Italy, is Italian.

clue.text: A clime so atrocious called for special wear for women

indicators.note: atrocious signals the letters of a clime so are badly mangled into a new order

explanation.surface: A dreadful climate demanded special clothes for women.
explanation.walkthrough: 'atrocious' rearranges ACLIMESO; 'called for' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A loose sleeveless undergarment or top is a piece of women's clothing.

clue.text: Arrives once more for the fruit-harvesting?

parts.note: to reap is to harvest a crop
pears are a fruit

explanation.surface: Someone turns up again for the fruit picking.
explanation.walkthrough: The hyphenated 'fruit-harvesting' is read as harvesting fruit: REAP then PEARS.
explanation.definitionFit: To come back into view is to show up again, i.e. arrive once more.

clue.text: Note fall in cereal production

parts.note: G is a musical note
rain is a fall from the sky

explanation.surface: A drop in the output of cereal farming is reported.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fall' reads as a decline, but it is rainfall; 'in' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Wheat, oats and barley seed is what cereal crops yield.

clue.text: Blow hot and cold, as the French say, with a woman

parts.note: dit is French for says or said
her refers to a woman

explanation.surface: A Frenchman's remark about a woman keeps changing.
explanation.walkthrough: DIT is French for 'says'; 'with' joins it to HER.
explanation.definitionFit: To blow hot and cold is an idiom for wavering indecisively.

clue.text: A bitter harangue to help backward people

indicators.note: backward means the word for to help is written from right to left

parts.note: aid means to help
a tribe is a people

explanation.surface: A rant about a backward community gets a hostile reception.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to help backward people' reads as charity for the underdeveloped, but 'backward' is the reversal signal on 'to help'.
explanation.definitionFit: A furious verbal attack or long denunciation is a rant.

clue.text: From habit about a hundred make apology

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so one piece goes round the other

parts.note: ex is Latin for from
use means custom or habit
C is the Roman numeral for a hundred

explanation.surface: Someone breaking a long habit says sorry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts C inside EXUSE; 'make' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A reason offered to justify a fault is a plea of regret, a kind of apology.

clue.text: Firm set against a high-minded individual, a hard worker

parts.note: con means against, as in pros and cons
ST is short for saint, a high-minded individual
the ant is proverbially industrious

explanation.surface: A company stands opposed to an idealist who works very hard.
explanation.walkthrough: 'set' is a link; ST is the saint abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: Steady and unchanging is a synonym of firm, as in firm loyalty.

clue.text: Show record drop

parts.note: a disc is a gramophone record
to drop something is to lose it

explanation.surface: A gig at which a record is dropped.
explanation.definitionFit: To reveal is to show, a synonym.

clue.text: A good painter does flat

parts.note: to do someone is to cheat, or con, them
a table is a flat surface

explanation.surface: An artist of quality paints an apartment.
explanation.walkthrough: John Constable was an English landscape painter; 'does' is slang for swindles.
explanation.definitionFit: John Constable was an English landscape artist of note.

clue.text: Bed-sit by the Avon which is barely used?

parts.note: Bath is a city on the River Avon in England
a bed-sit is a single room

explanation.surface: Lodgings by an English river that hardly anyone uses.
explanation.walkthrough: 'barely' is the pun: a place used naked. BATH is the English spa city on the Avon; 'by' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A room for washing is where people are unclothed, so used 'barely'.

clue.text: Countryman taking a cad in-an error

indicators.note: error signals that the letters of a cad in an are wrongly arranged

explanation.surface: A compatriot lets a scoundrel in by mistake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'error' rearranges ACADINAN; 'taking' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A person from Canada is a compatriot of that country, a countryman.

clue.text: Jemmy's triumph over lawyers

parts.note: to crow is to exult in triumph
the bar is the legal profession of barristers

explanation.surface: A burglar's tool wins a victory over the legal profession.
explanation.walkthrough: A jemmy is a British word for a short prying bar used by burglars; 'over' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A jemmy is a short iron lever for forcing doors.

clue.text: Some like to paint, entirely absorbed

indicators.note: some means only part of the words paint, entirely is taken

explanation.surface: Certain people love painting with total concentration.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Some' takes letters from 'paINT ENTirely'; 'like to' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Fully concentrated or engrossed is a synonym of absorbed.

clue.text: Abuse one gets in some occupations

indicators.note: gets in means one piece enters the other

parts.note: trades are jobs or occupations
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Someone receives insults in certain jobs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gets in' puts I inside TRADES; 'some' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Long angry speeches are verbal attacks, i.e. abuse.

clue.text: Sweeping away the Tories?

parts.note: out means away, not at home
the Tories are the political right

explanation.surface: Throwing the Conservatives out of office.
explanation.walkthrough: TORIES are the British Conservative party, of the political right.
explanation.definitionFit: Complete or total, as in a sweeping victory.

clue.text: Riled maybe to find a person wasting time

indicators.note: maybe suggests the letters of riled could be put another way

explanation.surface: An angry state discovered in a time-waster.
explanation.walkthrough: 'maybe' rearranges RILED; 'to find' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A lazybones who does nothing is one who wastes time.

clue.text: Older school-head, exceptionally alert

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter
exceptionally signals the letters of alert are put in an unusual order

explanation.surface: An elder headteacher is unusually alert.
explanation.walkthrough: 'head' takes S from school; 'exceptionally' rearranges ALERT.
explanation.definitionFit: Less fresh with time is a sense of older, as with bread.

clue.text: Don't take a holiday

explanation.surface: An instruction not to go away on vacation.
explanation.definitionFit: To leave something is to not take it; leave is also time off work, a vacation.

clue.text: The period is certainly right

annotationWithheld.why: Clue 'The period is certainly right' (4) as held gives no parse for TEAR: ERA plus R leaves T unexplained; likely OCR garble or a mismatched clue.

clue.text: To reject a coin is quite commonplace

parts.note: to ban is to reject or forbid
L stands for libra, the pound coin

explanation.surface: Turning down a coin is very ordinary.
explanation.walkthrough: L is the old abbreviation for a pound (libra), here a coin.
explanation.definitionFit: Trite and unoriginal is a synonym of commonplace.

clue.text: Superior directors in deep water

parts.note: over means above or superior
a board is a group of company directors

explanation.surface: Senior executives find themselves in serious trouble.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in deep water' looks like trouble, but means over the side into the sea.
explanation.definitionFit: Over the side of a ship into the sea is in the water.

clue.text: Dealing with code-not so hard

parts.note: re means about or concerning
Morse is the dots-and-dashes telegraph code
less means not so much

explanation.surface: Handling a code is not all that difficult.
explanation.definitionFit: Pitiless and unrelenting is a synonym of hard-hearted, hard.
